extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and other stakeholders who submit or comment on USPTO information collections relating to patent term extension and patent term adjustment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal requirements for submitting patent term extension and patent term adjustment applications, interim extension requests, petitions (reconsideration, reinstatement, withdrawal), and for commenting on the USPTO's information collection (OMB Control No. 0651-0020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term restoration eligibility (35 U.S.C. 156)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only patents for drug products, medical devices, food additives, or color additives are potentially eligible for extension; the maximum length that a patent may be extended under 35 U.S.C. 156 is 5 years. The USPTO administers 35 U.S.C. 156 through 37 CFR 1.710-1.791.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to products regulated by FDA or USDA; extensions are statutory and capped at 5 years. See 37 CFR 1.710-1.791 for procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents required under 35 U.S.C. 156(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent term extension must: identify the approved product; the patent to be extended; and the claims included in the patent that cover the approved product, a method of using the approved product, or a method of manufacturing the approved product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 156(d) also requires submission of information that enables the USPTO to determine (1) eligibility of the patent for extension, (2) the rights that will be derived from the extension, and (3) the period of extension. The applicant must also provide a brief description of the activities undertaken by the applicant during the regulatory review period with respect to the approved product and the significant dates of these activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension criteria (35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5) and 156(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5), an interim extension may be granted if the applicable regulatory review period that began for a product is reasonably expected to extend beyond the expiration of the patent term in effect. Under 35 U.S.C. 156(e)(2), an interim extension may be granted if the term of an eligible patent for which an application for patent term extension has been submitted would expire before a certificate of extension is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information collection covers initial and subsequent applications for interim extensions (see Table 1 items: Initial Application for Interim Extension under 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5); Subsequent Application for Interim Extension under 37 CFR 1.790). Fees, estimated response counts, and estimated hours are provided for these items (e.g., filing fees and time estimates in Table 1 and Table 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for review of final eligibility decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The information collection covers requests for review of final eligibility decisions under the patent term extension provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions are reflected in the burden table (e.g., 'Petition to review final Eligibility Decision Under 37 CFR 1.750' with estimated respondents and time per response). Fees and estimated costs are shown in the notice (see Table 1 and Table 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to withdraw an application after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection covers requests to withdraw an application requesting a patent term extension after it is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate line item in the burden estimates ('Declaration to Withdraw an Application to Extend Patent Term') includes estimated counts, time per response, and associated cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment eligibility and causes (35 U.S.C. 154)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may adjust the term of an original patent under 35 U.S.C. 154 due to certain delays in the prosecution of the patent application, including delays caused by interference proceedings, secrecy orders, or appellate review by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or a Federal court reversing an adverse USPTO determination of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO administers 35 U.S.C. 154 through 37 CFR 1.701-1.705. The information collection covers information gathered in requests related to patent term adjustments under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reconsideration of patent term adjustment determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent term provisions of 35 U.S.C. 154(b) allow the applicant an opportunity to request reconsideration of the USPTO's patent term adjustment determination; this collection covers information gathered in such a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflected in burden estimates as 'Petition for Reconsideration of Patent Term Adjustment Determination' with an estimated 622 respondents, 25 hours per response, and filing fee amounts shown in Table 1/2; estimated annual respondent cost burden provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of granted patent term adjustment and petition for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may reduce the amount of a granted patent term adjustment if delays were caused by an applicant's failure to make a reasonable effort to respond to a communication from the USPTO within three months of the communication's mailing date. Applicants may petition for reinstatement of a reduction in patent term adjustment with a showing that, in spite of all due care, the applicant was unable to respond to a communication within the three-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A line item ('Petition for Reinstatement of Reduced Patent Term Adjustment') is included in estimated burdens and fees. The petitioner must show 'despite all due care' to overcome the reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of submission for information collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Items in this information collection may be submitted electronically, by mail, or by hand delivery to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO prefers electronic submission; the notice estimates that 1% of items will be mailed and provides postage cost estimates. The agency also explicitly invites electronic submission as a way to minimize burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Control Number and administrative metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Control Number: 0651-0020. Forms: None. Type of Review: Extension and revision of a currently approved information collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected Public: Private sector. Respondent's Obligation: Required to obtain or retain benefits. Frequency: On occasion. These administrative attributes frame applicability and mandatory nature of responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated burden, responses, time, and cost metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated Number of Annual Respondents: 903; Estimated Number of Annual Responses: 903; Estimated Time per Response: 1 to 25 hours; Estimated Total Annual Respondent Burden Hours: 6,807 hours; Estimated Total Annual Respondent Hourly Cost Burden: $3,042,729; Estimated Total Annual Respondent Non-hourly Cost Burden: $489,431.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed per-item burden table (Table 1) lists items such as 'Application to Extend Patent Term Under 35 U.S.C. 156' (134 responses, 25 hours each), 'Petition for Reconsideration' (622 responses, 25 hours each), filing fees per item (Table 2), and postage assumptions. Use these numbers when assessing paperwork burden and estimated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee schedule for listed items
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing fees are specified for particular items (e.g., Application to Extend Patent Term under 35 U.S.C. 156: $2,500; Initial Application for Interim Extension under 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(5): $1,320; Petition for Reconsideration of Patent Term Adjustment Determination: $226, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 provides fee codes, annual estimated responses, and total cost per item; total estimated annual filing fees are listed (Totals: $489,330). Fees vary by item and are part of the non-hourly cost burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and public availability of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit Confidential Business Information or otherwise sensitive or protected information. All comments submitted in response to this notice are a matter of public record and may be made publicly available at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before including an address, phone number, email address, or other personally identifiable information (PII) in a comment, be advised the entire comment—including PII—may be made publicly available. One may request withholding PII from public view, but the USPTO cannot guarantee it will be able to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics USPTO solicits for public comment (four review objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is soliciting public comments to: (a) Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information will have practical utility; (b) Evaluate the accuracy of the Agency's estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used; (c) Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (d) Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology, e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should address one or more of these four points when submitting feedback. The agency will include or summarize each comment in its request to OMB to approve the information collection.
